State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Sony India Pvt. Ltd. vs Gurpreet Singh on 6 November, 2015
2nd Additional Bench

STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION,
PUNJAB, DAKSHIN MARG, SECTOR 37-A, CHANDIGARH.

 First Appeal No.44 of 2015

 Date of institution : 14.01.2015
 Date of decision : 06.11.2015

 Sony India Pvt. Ltd. Registered Office at A-31, Mohan
 Cooperative Industrial Estate Mathura Road, New Delhi-110044
 through its Authorised Signatory.

 .......Appellant/OP No.3
 Versus

 1. Gurpreet Singh son of Sh. Baldev Singh Resident of 27370 Lal
 Singh Nagar, Bathinda, Punjab.
 ........Respondent/Complainant

 2. ADEV Electronics 20, Krishna Market Bibi Wala Road, Bathinda,
 through its Proprietor/Partner.

 .......ProformaRespondents/OppositePartiesNo.2

 First Appeal against the order dated
 16.10.2014 passed by the District
 Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum,
 Bathinda.
Quorum:-

 Shri Gurcharan Singh Saran, Presiding Judicial Member
 Smt. Surinder Pal Kaur, Member

Present:-

 For the appellant :Sh. Amit Arora, Advocate
 For respondent No.1 :Sh. Siddharth Gupta, Advocate
 For respondent No.2 :Service Dispensed with.

MRS. SURINDER PAL KAUR, Member

 ORDER
The appellant/OP NO3(hereinafter referred as "OP") has filed
F.A. No. 44 of 2015 2
the present appeal against the order dated 16.10.2014 passed by

District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Bathinda (hereinafter

referred as "District Forum") in Consumer Complaint No.411 dated

09.07.2014 vide which complaint filed by the respondent/complainant

(hereinafter referred as complainant) was allowed against OP No 2&3.

They were directed to refund the price of the mobile handset i.e.

Rs.40,000/- and Rs.5,000/- as compensation, failing which, OPs were

liable to pay interest @ 9% p.a. from the date of deposit of mobile

handset with OP No.2 till payment. It was also directed to complainant to

hand over the mobile set along with accessories to OPNO 2&3.
2. A complaint was filed by the complainant under
Section 12
of

the Consumer Protection Act 1986(in short `the Act') against OPs on the

averments that OP No.3 had launched a new mobile handset, having

model no. Sony Xperia C-6902 ZI, and advertised through various

channels. The said handset was dust and water resistant/ water proof

even if the same was kept in water. Mobile handset was having

IP55/IP58 impressive rating, which make the set slim and sleek

Smartphone. Being allured by advertisements of OPNO3, complainant

purchased one mobile set Sony Xperia C-6902 ZI having IMEI

No.358094052941706 manufactured by OP No.3, from OP No.1 vide Bill

no.2508 dated 23.12.2013 for a sum of Rs.40,000/-. OP No.1 had

assured that said handset was having best quality and mobile set was

under one year warranty. After purchasing the mobile set complainant

started using the same. Complainant had gone to Maclodgunj (H.P.) due

to summer vacation, when he was in market suddenly rain started and

he put his mobile set in pocket of his pent and rushed towards his room.

After reaching the room he dried the cover and other area where water

could enter. Due to moisture in mobile set clarity of picture had come
F.A. No. 44 of 2015 3
down and volume/Zoom key was not working. He was unable to

download any application. Complainant put the mobile set in his pocket

as the company had assured that mobile set was water proof. On

30.06.2014, complainant visited in office of OP No.2 and enquired about

defect in mobile set. After checking OP No.2 said that handset was

defected due to water and it was out of warranty. Complainant informed

OP No.2 that they assured that handset was water proof and could be

used in extreme weather conditions like snow and rain. OP No.2 had

retained mobile set against job card No.W114063002470 dated

30.6.2014 and asked the complainant to enquire next day. On 01.07.2014

OP No.2 returned handset with excuse that it was out of warranty though

the same was purchased on 23.12.2013. However, OP No.2 had

informed the complainant that if he wanted to swap mobile set he had to

pay 80% on MRP. The above said act of OPs amounted to deficiency in

service and unfair trade practice on their part. Hence, he filed the

complaint before the District Forum seeking following directions against

OPs:-
(i) to replace the defective handset with new one or to refund

 Rs.40,000/-i.e. (price of mobile)
(ii) to pay Rs.20,000/- as compensation for mental tension and

 harassment
(iii) to pay Rs. 5500/- as litigation costs.
3. Complaint was contested by OPNO 1 to 3 who filed joint

written reply by taking preliminary objections that connectors/ports of

mobile set were not properly closed at the time of incident. Mobile set

was damaged due to liquid. There was no warranty as mobile set was

damaged due to negligence of complainant. As a goodwill gesture OPs

had offered to complainant a special discount for exchange of mobile set
F.A. No. 44 of 2015 4
i.e. 20% on MRP. But complainant had refused to accept the offer and

wanted to repair mobile-set free of costs against warranty conditions.

However, this handset was certified by international bodies for certain

standards relating to water and dust resistance and on basis of this OP

No.3 claimed that mobile set was water proof and dust resistance. Under

terms and conditions of warranty, OPs were not liable to repair and

replace the handset, as the product was out off warranty. On merits, OPs

admitted that complainant had purchased Sony Xperia ZI mobile phone

bearing model noC6902 on 23.12.2013 for a sum of Rs 40,000. It was

pleaded that mobile phone was water resistant not water proof. It was

denied that there was manufacturing defect in handset. Complainant had

filed the complaint only to harass them. There was no deficiency in their

service and prayed for dismissal of the complaint with costs.

4 The parties were allowed by the learned District Forum to lead

their evidence.
5. In support of the averments, the complainant had tendered into

evidence his affidavit Ex C-1 along with other documents Ex.C-2 to Ex.C-

7and closed their evidence. On other hand OPs had tendered into

evidence affidavit of Priyank Chauhan s/o Ram Pal Singh, Sony India

Private Ltd. as Ex.OP-3/1 along with documents Ex.OP-3/2 to Ex.OP-3/7

and closed their evidence.
6. After going through the allegations alleged in the complaint,

written reply filed by OPs evidence and documents brought on the record,

the learned District Forum allowed the complaint as referred above.
7. Aggrieved against the order passed by the Ld. District Forum,

the appellant/OP NO3 has preferred the present appeal.
8. It was submitted by the learned counsel for OP that District

Forum failed to consider that warranty was subject to terms and
F.A. No. 44 of 2015 5
conditions. Under warranty terms company was only liable to repair and

replace the defective part. Hand set was water and dust resistant and the

same fact was advertised on television. There was no expert report to

prove that mobile set was having manufacturing defect. Mobile had

damaged due to ingression of liquid. Thus OP was not liable for such type

of defect. He prayed for to set-aside impugned order and acceptance of

appeal.
9. Whereas, counsel for the complainant has submitted that the

complainant has used the mobile set as per literature and in case defect

has occurred during warranty period, OPs are liable to rectify or replace

the same. OPs have failed to prove that complainant has misused the

mobile set. Therefore, the District Forum had returned the correct findings

and prayed for to uphold the impugned order.
9. Complainant had purchased one Sony Xperia ZI C6902 smart

phone from OP No.1. As per allegations of complainant when he had

gone to avail his summer vacations at Maclodgunj (HP) he was fixed in

rain and put his mobile set in the pocket and when he reached in room

then the mobile set was not properly working due to water. The counsel

for the complainant had referred the literature of this mobile set as Ex.C-4

as per literature mobile set is water proof, specific portion of the literature

is reproduced as under:
X X X X

 "The Sony Xperia Z1 has an impressive IP55/IP58 rating, which

makes this slim and sleek smartphone both waterproof (1) and resistant

to the tiniest dust particles". It was further mentioned as under:-
"With the waterproof (1) Xperia Z1, you can take pictures while

swimming upto 30 minutes. You can even dive up to 1.5 m with it. Just

remember that all the coordinator the micro USB port, the micro SIM slot,
F.A. No. 44 of 2015 6
the headphone jack and the memory card slot must be firmly closed".
Whereas, the counsel for the appellant has referred to a different

literature Ex.OP-3/7 which speaks only water resistance but this literature

pertains the mobile Sony C 6603/C 6602 which is a different type of

mobile set therefore this literature cannot be relied upon.

When defect had appeared in the set due to entering of water they are

required to rectify or replace it but they refused either to rectify or to

replace it which is contrary to the terms and conditions of the policy.
10. Further, a plea was taken by appellant/OP No.3 that there was

no expert report. When literature of the specific mobile set speaks that it

is water proof and defect occurred in mobile set due to entering of water

therefore reason for causing defect in the mobile set is clear. Therefore,

no other report was required to know the reason for defect in the mobile

set.
11. The other plea of the OPs that defect had occurred due to

mishandling of mobile set. There is no specific evidence placed on

record by OPs how the mobile set was misused by the complainant. As

per literature of OPs mobile set was water proof. Complainant had put the

mobile set in his pocket and some water had entered in the mobile set.

The District Forum has also relied upon the literature Ex.C-6 and came to

the conclusion that the mobile set sold to the complainant was water

proof and OP had failed to rectify or replace the set within the warranty

period as per terms and conditions of the policy. Literature referred by the

counsel for OP during the appeal is not relating to the mobile set

purchased by the complainant. However, the order of District Forum

ordering for refunding the cost of mobile set without any order to rectify

the defect or replacement of the mobile set is required to be modified.
12. In view of the above discussion the appeal of the
F.A. No. 44 of 2015 7
appellant/OP No.3 is partly allowed and impugned order is modified with

a direction to OP No.2 & 3 to rectify the defect in the mobile set to the

satisfaction of the complainant, in case defect is not curable then

replaces the mobile set. In case the same model of the mobile set is not

available then they are directed to refund the cost of the mobile set i.e.

Rs.40,000/- along with interest @ 9% from the date of filing the complaint

till actual payment.
13. The Appellant/OP No.3 had deposited a sum of Rs.23,550/- at

the time of filing of the appeal along with interest which had been accrued

thereon, if any, shall be remitted by the registry to Appellant/OP No.3 after

satisfaction of the complainant with regard to the rectification of Mobile set on

the application to be moved by the Appellant/OP No.3.
14. The arguments in this appeal were heard on 19.10.2015 and the

order was reserved. Now, the order be communicated to the parties as per

rules.
15. The appeal could not be decided within the statutory period

due to heavy pendency of court cases.
(GURCHARAN SINGH SARAN)
 Presiding Judicial Member
